articles.title: TikTok expands into restaurant guides with 'Must Eat' feature | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
TikTok has long been a go-to place for discovering new spots, with viral videos helping local restaurants attract new customers. Now, TikTok is making it easier for users to find their next favorite restaurant with a new feature called “Must Eat.”
Introduced Wednesday, the community-driven guide highlights restaurants getting attention on the platform, bringing food recommendations from across the U.S. into one place.
The move puts TikTok in more direct competition with platforms like Yelp and Google Maps. But instead of relying mainly on search results, maps, and traditional reviews, TikTok is building on what it already does well: connecting people with restaurants through recommendations shared by other users.
“Must Eat” uses more than 40 million posts and comments to pull restaurant recommendations and curated lists together in one place. Users can browse restaurants by city and filter results by cuisine, price, rating, and location, making it easier to compare options before heading out.
The recommendations are split into two categories: “Everyday Eats,” featuring casual favorites and neighborhood go-tos, and “Elevated Dining,” highlighting restaurants for celebrations, special occasions, or a night out.
Additionally, select restaurants can be booked directly through TikTok via OpenTable.

articles.title: Tandem Oled, 2000 nits : tout savoir sur l'écran ProLed XDR du nouveau MacBook Pro — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Apple a dévoilé ce mercredi 28 octobre, dans un communiqué, un MacBook Pro en 14 et 16 pouces. C’est le premier Mac équipé d’un écran OLED, baptisé PROLED XDR. Sur le papier, cette dalle offre deux fois plus de luminosité que l’écran Mini LED des MacBook Pro actuels en usage courant, et un contraste dix fois supérieur. Elle est aussi tactile, une première sur un Mac.
Apple garde pourtant les modèles Mini LED au catalogue, et l’OLED coûte au moins 400 euros de plus à puce égale.
Un écran Tandem Oled sur MacBook Pro
Apple parle d’OLED « tandem ». Comme sur un iPhone, chaque pixel produit sa propre lumière, mais la dalle empile deux couches lumineuses au lieu d’une. Les deux couches se partagent le travail. La dalle peut donc monter plus haut en luminosité sans pousser chaque couche à fond, ce qui limite aussi leur usure. Apple utilise déjà cette technique sur l’iPad Pro depuis mai 2024, et LG Display en a même fait une appellation à part pour ses dalles de moniteurs. Côté Mac, la marque y pense depuis au moins 2019, quand elle négociait avec Samsung Display pour passer ses MacBook Pro à l’OLED.
Apple annonce jusqu’à 2 000 nits, en HDR comme en SDR. Le contraste, c’est-à-dire l’écart entre le noir le plus profond et le blanc le plus lumineux, atteint 10 000 000:1. L’écran garde ProMotion, le rafraîchissement variable d’Apple. Il monte à 120 Hz pour les contenus les plus dynamiques et descend jusqu’à 10 Hz sur une image ou un contenu fixe, afin d’économiser la batterie.

articles.title: Can This Vermont Company Remake the Electric Aviation Industry?
articles.summary:
How Beta Technologies Is Clearing the Runway for Electric Flight
It aims to lift the industry with its aircraft, motors, batteries, and charging network
In the cockpit of Beta Technologies’ Alia CX300, pilot Chris Caputo steers onto Runway 33 at Patrick Leahy Burlington International Airport in Vermont. Cleared for takeoff, he releases the brakes and nudges the throttle forward.
At the back of the aircraft, the five-blade pusher propeller snaps awake, and the Alia bolts forward. There’s no shriek of a turbofan spooling up, no shudder of a piston engine, and no wait for thrust. Just the low hum of an electric motor and a shove of instant acceleration.
Within a few seconds, we’re at 85 knots (almost 160 kilometers per hour), and Caputo rotates the nose upward. The runway drops abruptly away as we climb. Gaining speed and altitude, we head northwest over Lake Champlain. Through the wraparound canopy, I watch the hunched shoulders of Vermont’s Green Mountains shrink under the right wing, with New York’s taller Adirondacks to the left.
Caputo, a former Air Force fighter pilot, flicks the control stick hard left, then right. Despite its 15-meter wingspan, the Alia feels snappy, its fly-by-wire system automatically coordinating aileron and rudder inputs. The machine, he says, is much simpler to manage than the Cessna 182 I flew around Australia in my student-pilot days.

articles.summary:
Android 18: Neue Funktion soll deine Kontakte besser schützen
In Android 18 schließt Google nach Jahren ein Einfallstor für Manipulationen im Adressbuch. Im kommenden Betriebssystem sollen Apps nicht mehr ohne die aktive Zustimmung der Nutzer:innen auf die Kontakte in deinem Smartphone zugreifen.
Dies erklärte Mishaal Rahman, der bei Google als Community-Manager für Android zuständig ist, in einem ausführlichen Thread bei X. Google hatte bereits am 21. Oktober 2026 Änderungen beim Zugriff auf das Adressbuch angekündigt. Für Rahman ging dieses wichtige Update dabei jedoch unter.
Android: App-Berechtigung als Freifahrtsschein
Bisher galt ein im Rückblick verblüffend sorgloses Prinzip. Hattest du einer App über die entsprechende Berechtigung einmal gestattet, auf dein Adressbuch zuzugreifen, konnte sie dort tun und lassen, was sie wollte. Ohne dass du davon etwas mitbekommen hast. Selbst Apps, die nur einen einzigen Kontakt hinzufügen wollten, hatten vollen Zugriff.
Dies bedeutete, dass böswillige Anwendungen oder manipulierte Apps etwa die Handynummern deiner Kontakte ändern konnten. Wenn dann deine Bank anrief, konnte es sein, dass du mit Betrügerinnen sprichst.

articles.title: El Niño pourrait provoquer une nouvelle flambée des concentrations de CO2, alerte l'OMM
articles.summary:
La Nasa a prévenu, nous nous dirigeons vraisemblablement vers un épisode d’El Niño « historique » dans l’océan Pacifique. Le phénomène est officiellement de retour depuis l’été, et selon l’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM), El Niño va se maintenir jusqu’en février 2027. Cet épisode s’annonce particulièrement intense. Une étude publiée cet été concluait même qu’El Niño est plus puissant qu’à aucun moment depuis 1 000 ans.
Une « nouvelle flambée » des gaz à effet de serre à craindre à cause d’El Niño
Ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, l’OMM a de nouveau attiré l’attention sur l’impact potentiel de ce phénomène, en lien avec un autre triste record planétaire. « Les concentrations de gaz à effet de serre ont atteint de nouveaux records, scellant ainsi une hausse des températures à long terme. L’intensification du phénomène El Niño pourrait entraîner une nouvelle flambée de ces concentrations », résume l’organisme des Nations unies sur X.
El Niño est un phénomène climatique naturel. Il se manifeste par des anomalies de températures de surface dans l’océan Pacifique équatorial. Ces températures plus chaudes que la normale peuvent entraîner une cascade d’effets sur la planète. Avec le réchauffement planétaire, ces effets peuvent être encore plus dommageables.

articles.title: Systems Thinking Is Vital in the Age of AI
articles.summary:
Modern engineering projects increasingly combine human judgment with machine capability. An engineer can define a problem, then ask an artificial intelligence tool to search relevant research and technical standards, generate design options, test them in simulation, and compare the results. The engineer can then bring the results to specialists who understand the parts AI cannot judge on its own, such as whether a design can be built safely, whether it makes sense in a particular setting, or how it might affect its users. The final decision about whether and how to move forward remains a human responsibility.
AI can help engineers do early project steps that once required several people with different technical skills. The engineer’s role is therefore expanding from performing each technical step to deciding how people, machines, and specialists’ knowledge should work together on the project.
The problem, not the title
Engineering has always been divided into disciplines, and for good reasons. Electrical, mechanical, civil, software, and other engineering fields require deep knowledge that takes years to develop. AI does not replace that need. It simply changes how easily engineers can explore the parts of a problem that sit outside their own specialty.
Consider a software engineer working on a medical device. AI can help the engineer review relevant biomedical research, understand unfamiliar terms, analyze data, and build an early model.

articles.title: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Nvidia on Wednesday released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free, open-weight model that transcribes audio in up to 40 languages. It also released version 2 of Granary, its open source speech dataset.
Nvidia boasts that Nemotron 3.5 can translate 31 languages to and from English, handle recordings up to an hour long, and tell up to eight speakers apart. It claims to beat rivals on benchmarks, including Hugging Face’s Open ASR Leaderboard.
These tools target developers building apps for business meetings and medical transcription, two of AI’s most established footholds in the workplace. Nvidia says developers can use the model, the updated Granary dataset, and tools like its NeMo Speech model to customize apps to recognize an industry’s jargon in each language. One drawback: Transcribe works with recorded audio, not livestreams.
Still, the company promises Transcribe, at 30 billion parameters, can run on a single chip, from the Jetson AGX Thor robotics controller and DGX Spark chip powering new laptops, to Blackwell datacenter chips. It joins Nvidia’s open-weight voice models, including the super small yet powerful Parakeet (1.1 billion parameters).
Nvidia’s latest voice entry comes during a busy period of AI voice releases: Mistral shipped Voxtral 3 earlier this month; ElevenLabs launched Realtime for instant speech in voice agents; and Salesforce released Launa-Omni, its voice model.

Our vision: From idea to completed software
The SDLC is no longer a linear path from planning to coding to testing to deployment. A code change, a request from a colleague, or a production metric can trigger work anywhere in the system. Most of us (and our agents) jump between different stages, depending on the task at hand. Developers set the direction, make decisions, and stay accountable for what ships. Velocity: get from idea to completed software as quickly, efficiently, and cost-effectively as possible

It impacts Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. With specially crafted compressed data, an attacker could crash the application, expose the contents of its memory, and potentially execute arbitrary code.

CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to the KEV catalog on October 27, but provided no information on the attacks. Federal civilian agencies have been instructed to address the flaw by November 10.

articles.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
articles.summary:
Advanced packaging requires models to cross company boundaries without exposing proprietary processes, but hiding too much can make the prediction break down.
Key Takeaways:
The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. But advanced packaging is making that separation much harder to maintain.
For years, engineers moved much of what they needed between companies through datasheets, design rules, and qualification specs, while the manufacturing knowledge stayed with the supplier. That arrangement held as long as the pieces behaved independently, but what one company keeps inside its process now shapes how another company’s part of the package performs once everything is assembled. As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

Artificial Intelligence
Distributed training with Ray Train DLCs and EFA on EKS
What usually stops PyTorch training from scaling out to a cluster is the container, not the model code. Every container needs the same CUDA runtime, a PyTorch build compiled against it, NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communications Library), the Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) userspace libraries, the AWS OFI NCCL plugin that connects NCCL to EFA, and a Ray version the cluster operator agrees with. Building that image and rebuilding it each time one of those pieces moves is a project of its own, and it has nothing to do with the model you set out to train. The Ray Train Deep Learning Container (DLC) is that image, built by AWS. AWS assembles the stack, tests it as one unit, publishes it in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) Public and keeps it patched.
Ray runs a job across machines as a single cluster with two roles. The Ray head coordinates and runs the global control store that tracks cluster state, the dashboard and job server you submit jobs to. Ray worker nodes supply the GPUs and run the training processes. Each worker joins the cluster by connecting to the head’s address when it starts. On Kubernetes, each of these is a pod. Kubernetes has no built-in idea of a Ray cluster, so something must create the head and worker pods, start Ray in the right role in each, point the workers at the head, and replace pods that fail. New generation FPGA announcements do not come often, which makes this a bit exciting for us. Today, Altera is introducing the Agilex 27 as the first family in its new Agilex 2X portfolio. Agilex 27 pairs hardened 800GbE and 1.6TbE Ethernet with PCIe 6.0 and 7.0 support, and offers configurable transceivers up to 256Gbps. What is more exciting, and what I learned on the pre-briefing call, is that Altera also has a new AI-assisted mode for putting these FPGAs to use.
HyperFlow and Third-Generation HyperFlex
A major new feature of the Agilex 27 family is HyperFlow. HyperFlow is a new full-chip distributed data network that Altera says can move data at multi-terabit-per-second rates throughout the FPGA. That traffic runs on a dedicated network instead of the programmable fabric, so it does not consume soft logic resources or add routing congestion. That leaves more FPGA resources for the application. As an example, a 1.6TbE Ethernet port can bring traffic in through hardened I/O, HyperFlow can carry it across the chip, and the soft logic can spend its resources on processing rather than moving data.
The new family has memory controllers for DDR5, LPDDR4, LPDDR5X, and LPDDR6. It also supports UCIe, has crypto acceleration, and Arm Cortex-A720 and Cortex-A520 cores. If you’ve tried to get an agent into production, the model and tool use are not the blocker. The main bottleneck is everything around them: how many teams can build within a secure environment, which team owns each model and tool, how AgentOps and error handling stay inside a pre-defined boundary, and how platform, Workstream, and finance teams see cost and health across accounts. For a Platform team that wants to support many agentic use cases, that’s a platform product to design and operate. In this post, we refer to the team that manages the platform as the Platform team, and to the teams that build on it as Workstream teams. Workstream teams are the domain or product teams that build and own agents on the platform.
Each Workstream team needs a paved road with approved models and tools, short-lived workload identity, isolated runtime and memory, automated evaluation, rollback, telemetry, and cost attribution. These controls need to remain consistent as Workstream teams customize prompts, tools, data access, and application behavior. When every team assembles them, controls drift, shared services become a bottleneck, and ownership is difficult to audit.

Elad Gil, a returning investor from the Series A, led the round. Gradient and Y Combinator also back the company. The Series B round brings the total funding to nearly $60 million.
Infisical provides tools for managing secrets, encryption keys, and digital certificates, along with privileged access management, covering cloud, on-premises, and AI infrastructure.

articles.title: A hidden ocean change near Antarctica could have global consequences
articles.summary:
The rapid decline of Antarctic sea ice since 2016 has triggered a dramatic shift in a crucial part of Earth’s climate system, scientists say.
In a paper published Wednesday, researchers documented a sharp salinity increase in a vast layer of the Southern Ocean, extending from 2,300 to 4,000 feet deep and encircling Antarctica. The shift reverses decades of freshening and echoes ocean changes usually associated with major global climate shifts over millennia but is now happening in just a few years.
The switch from a decades-long trend of freshening water to increasing salinity has implications that could extend beyond Antarctica. The layer, known as Antarctic Intermediate Water, spreads northward into the Indian, Pacific, and Atlantic oceans, transporting heat, carbon, oxygen, and nutrients toward the tropics, and even across the equator, said co-author Bishakhdatta Gayen, a researcher and professor at the University of Melbourne and at the Centre for Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences in Bengaluru, India.
Gayen said the study combined six independent datasets to track changes in the Southern Ocean from 2004 to 2024. The data came from Argo floats, which drift through the ocean and periodically descend to different depths to measure water properties such as density and salinity, then resurface to transmit the readings. A 2025 study also detected increasing surface salinity linked to declining sea ice, he added.

articles.summary:
UEFI-Lücke: Kritischer Bug versteckt sich seit 16 Jahren in vielen Servern
Erst Mitte Oktober 2026 sorgte die Entdeckung schwerwiegender Sicherheitslücken in der weit verbreiteten Programmiersprache PHP für Aufregung. Angreifer:innen sollen die php2shell genannten Schwachstellen schon aktiv ausnutzen und versuchen, ganze Server zu kapern. Allein in Deutschland sollen vier Millionen Dienste betroffen sein.
Schwachstelle in Baustein für UEFI-Firmware
Jetzt ist eine weitere kritische Sicherheitslücke bekannt geworden, von der ein großer Teil der Server weltweit betroffen sein soll. Dabei handelt es sich um eine Schwachstelle in EDK II, dem Open-Source-Code, der vielen UEFI-Firmwares als Basis dient. Diese Firmware ist der moderne Nachfolger von BIOS und startet beim Einschalten eines Computers als erstes, noch vor dem Betriebssystem. Laut Ars Technica setzen die meisten UEFI-Anbieter wie AMI, Insyde und Phoenix auf den Code.
Die Sicherheitslücke in EDK II (CVE-2026-97631), die auf der Schweregradskala CVSS 4.0 9,5 von 10 Punkten erreicht, befindet sich konkret im ICMP-Code des PXE-Netzwerkstarts. PXE sorgt dafür, dass Computer über ein Netzwerk statt von einer eingebauten Festplatte oder SSD starten. In Unternehmen dient diese Funktion dazu, viele Rechner zentral einzurichten oder zu warten.

articles.title: AI agents need to be replaceable – without losing your work
articles.summary:
AI agents need to be replaceable – without losing your work
An agent receives approval to process a partial refund. It sends the request to a payment API, and the process crashes. Maybe the payment service completed the refund. Maybe the request never went through. A replacement agent spins up and finds an operation record marked dispatched with no outcome written.
This kind of ambiguity isn’t unique to agents. Any distributed worker crashing mid-mutation faces the same problem. But a conventional worker resumes a predetermined workflow from the last checkpoint. An agent does something more dangerous: it reasons on its own. Given the same customer request and no outcome record, it might come up with a different plan, pick different parameters, or decide to issue a new refund instead of continuing the one already approved.
“An agent does something more dangerous: it reasons on its own.”
If the original refund went through, a second attempt refunds the customer twice. The charge still has enough remaining balance to cover another partial refund, so nothing stops it.
The replacement must inherit the original operation, not reinterpret it.
The operation must outlive the agent
An agent’s process, its in-memory variables, its transient reasoning context: all disposable. The business operation is not. The refund, its approval, its parameters, its current status. articles.title: 1 147 pages d'une complexité « redoutable » : les physiciens refusent de publier trop tôt la preuve d'OpenAI malgré l'appel des mathématiciens
articles.summary:
Une preuve scientifique d’une longueur et d’une complexité remarquables. C’est ainsi qu’ont réagi les cinq physiciens à la lecture de la démonstration écrite par un modèle d’intelligence artificielle de la société américaine OpenAI, au sujet de l’un des sept grands problèmes du prix du millénaire : la théorie de Yang-Mills.
OpenAI affirme que son modèle a prouvé l’existence de la théorie quantique de Yang-Mills sur le plan mathématique.
Cette théorie est la base de la chromodynamique quantique, qui décrit l’interaction nucléaire forte. C’est elle qui colle les quarks entre eux. Les quarks sont les briques des protons et des neutrons, au cœur des noyaux atomiques.
Ces cinq scientifiques, sollicités par OpenAI pour analyser les travaux de ce modèle d’IA, ne se prononcent pas à ce stade sur la véracité de la preuve. Dans leur communiqué commun, publié ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, ils se contentent d’en noter les contours : on parle d’un document long de 1 147 pages et d’une technicité manifeste. D’où leur réaction initiale.

articles.title: Echte Polwanderung: Warum selbst der geografische Nordpol keinen festen Platz hat
articles.summary:
10 Zentimeter pro Jahr: Warum selbst der geografische Nordpol keinen festen Platz hat
Die geografischen Pole der Erde verschieben sich derzeit mit einer per Satellit gemessenen Geschwindigkeit von rund zehn Zentimetern pro Jahr, was die durchschnittliche Driftgeschwindigkeit tektonischer Platten übersteigt. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, handelt es sich bei solchen Geschwindigkeiten nicht bloß um kurzlebige Ausreißer der Gegenwart, da vergleichbare Verschiebungen in den vergangenen 320 Millionen Jahren mehrfach über Zeiträume von jeweils zehn Millionen Jahren auftraten.
Ein Forschungsteam um den Geowissenschaftler Mathew Domeier, den Geologen Leandro C. Gallo, die Geowissenschaftlerin Chloé M. Marcilly und den Geophysiker Trond H. Torsvik von der norwegischen Universität Oslo wies insgesamt vier solcher Phasen anhand urzeitlicher Meeresspiegelschwankungen nach. Diese Episoden lagen in den Zeitfenstern vor 200 bis 190 Millionen, vor 150 bis 140 Millionen, vor 100 bis 90 Millionen sowie vor 30 bis 20 Millionen Jahren und erreichten Raten von mindestens 0,6 Breitengraden pro einer Million Jahre, was mindestens 6,7 Zentimetern pro Jahr entspricht.

articles.title: Jedify formally launches Data Agents for building AI analysts in plain language - SiliconANGLE

Jedify formally launches Data Agents for building AI analysts in plain language
Enterprise artificial intelligence context startup Jedify Inc. today formally launched Data Agents, a product that lets business teams set up autonomous AI analysts by describing the work they want done in plain language.
Data Agents takes on a longstanding limit of business intelligence software, where analysts have to build dashboards ahead of time around the questions they expect people to ask. Generic AI assistants have tried to fill that gap. In Jedify’s telling, those tools end up guessing at what a business means from its raw tables and schemas.
The company’s core product is a context graph that pulls structured data and documents into a single model of how a business works, down to metric definitions and record-level permissions. Data Agents runs on top of it. Because joins and schema mapping are already worked out inside the graph, building an agent comes down to describing the question.
Users decide when an agent runs, whether on request, on a schedule or when a condition they have defined is met. A market that starts to underperform is the kind of anomaly an agent is meant to catch on its own, and Jedify’s deep research engine then works out what most likely drove the change.
Data access is tied to the person asking the question. Anything that user is barred from seeing, even a single row in a table, stays out of the agent’s results. On cost, Jedify claims its agents burn far fewer toke…

- Date:

- Source:

The breakthrough could pave the way for tiny, self-healing biological robots capable of exploring fragile environments that ordinary machines cannot safely navigate.
- Share:
A swimming robot does not necessarily need a bulky motor or powerful mechanical parts to move through water. MIT researchers have demonstrated that a single, carefully engineered layer of living muscle cells can generate enough force to propel a tiny robot forward.
The engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins. Described in a new study published in Advanced Functional Materials, the device has a flexible gel framework roughly the length and width of a stick of gum. The gel forms two fins, each coated with a layer of muscle cells far thinner than a human hair. These cells have been genetically modified to contract when exposed to light.
By directing light onto either fin, the researchers can trigger muscle contractions that make the fin flap and push the robot through water. Adjusting which fin receives light and how frequently it is illuminated allows the team to control both its speed and direction.

articles.summary:
LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years. As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom. It does not appear to be a 2-in-1 convertible design, though; all the footage was of people reaching up to touch the screen in a normal laptop configuration.
The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared. The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences. First, it’s much lighter. Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.

articles.title: Long-Hidden Flaws Patched in EPICS Research Facility Control Software

Four vulnerabilities in EPICS Base could allow attackers to crash processes in control systems used at particle accelerators, fusion experiments and other large research facilities. One flaw could potentially lead to code execution.
CISA disclosed the issues in an advisory published on Tuesday, saying they impact EPICS Base 7.0.10 and earlier. The agency recommends updating to version 7.0.11.
The vulnerabilities were discovered by Cipher, an autonomous security research system made by Causal Security.
EPICS is an open source software toolkit that scientific facilities rely on to build their control systems, and EPICS Base is its central component. According to Causal, ITER’s fusion reactor control system is based on EPICS, and the Advanced Photon Source at Argonne National Laboratory makes heavy use of it.
The most severe of the bugs is CVE-2026-114595 (CVSS score of 9.8), an integer overflow that can occur when network requests are processed. According to CISA, it can lead to a wrongly sized memory allocation, and processing attacker-supplied data afterwards could corrupt memory, trigger DoS, or possibly enable remote code execution.
Exploiting CVE-2026-114596 (CVSS score of 8.2) can cause an out-of-bounds write that leaves the process unstable or causes DoS. CVE-2026-114597 (CVSS score of 7.5) is an out-of-bounds read that could crash the application and leak data from nearby memory, while CVE-2026-114598 (CVSS score of 7.5) is a type confusion issue that can be triggered w…

Son doux nom ? CVE-2026-97631. Révélée le 22 octobre 2026, elle se loge dans le firmware de la plupart des serveurs, sous le système d’exploitation, dans des couches logicielles que personne ne voit jamais.

L’attaque se joue dans un laps de temps très réduit, pratiquement à l’instant où notre doigt lâche le bouton d’allumage. Quand on allume un serveur, le système d’exploitation n’est pas le premier programme à se lancer. Avant lui s’exécute le firmware, un logiciel stocké sur une puce de la carte mère, qui vérifie le matériel puis passe la main au système.
Sur les machines modernes, ce firmware suit une norme appelée UEFI. La plupart des fabricants le construisent à partir d’une même base de code open source, EDK2, que les grands fournisseurs du secteur comme AMI, Insyde ou Phoenix utilisent abondamment. Jusque-là, rien de compliqué.

articles.title: What happens when the agent is long gone, but its access key lives on?
articles.summary:
What happens when the agent is long gone, but its access key lives on?
Imagine: There’s a line on the credential report that no one on the platform team can explain. An IAM user called research-agent-2 has an access key created 14 months ago that was last used 11 months ago. And it’s still active.
The project it supported closed long ago, and the person who approved it doesn’t even work at the company anymore.
While this example is hypothetical, the lifecycle problem isn’t.
This doesn’t require carelessness. An agent is created for a task, the task ends, and nobody revisits its access. A departing person triggers offboarding; a finished agent just leaves a closed tab. AWS IAM user access keys don’t expire automatically, so a forgotten key stays valid until somebody disables or deletes it.
“A departing person triggers offboarding; a finished agent just leaves a closed tab.”
OWASP puts improper offboarding first in its 2025 Top 10 for non-human identities, and the remedy reads like this series’ premise: retire what’s no longer needed, and give the rest an accountable owner. The hard part is knowing what exists.
The problem is that attackers move faster than an annual audit ever could. In September 2026, GreyNoise documented an AI-orchestrated campaign against PaperCut servers: the attacker went from an empty workspace to remote code execution at a real victim in under four hours, and once launched, the campaign compromised at least eleven organizations in 26 seconds. articles.title: Nvidia launches a promptable transcription model

Nvidia launches a promptable transcription model
Nvidia on Wednesday launched Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, its latest multilingual transcription model. The new open-weight model, the company says, ranks first on Hugging Face’s Open ASR open model leaderboard for English, with an average word error rate of 5.33%, and also sits at the top of two speaker-attribution benchmarks.
But what’s maybe even more interesting is that this is a promptable transcription model. Being promptable here means that the user can give the model specific instructions before it listens. Typically, that means setting the context for the transcription by telling the model that a given audio file is a medical discussion in English, for example, and giving it a list of medical terms.
Users can also tell the model to label each speaker or ask it questions about the audio. They can request a verbatim transcript or a cleaned-up version, and tell it how to format numbers, for example.
Nvidia bundles these capabilities, along with translation, into a single checkpoint, which could simplify the work of building applications around them.
Ideally, setting this context reduces the error rate. The trade-off is that these models are much larger than traditional transcription models, which are often under a billion parameters in size. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is a 30B mixture-of-experts model with 4 billion active parameters.

articles.summary:
On Tuesday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed that hackers have begun exploiting a critical Brotli vulnerability known as Node2Shell, Broccoli2Shell, and HTTP2Shell.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, this critical-severity flaw stems from an out-of-bounds write weakness in the Brotli decoder used to expand data compressed with Google's widely popular Brotli lossless compression algorithm.
Unprivileged attackers can use a maliciously crafted Brotli-compressed stream to trigger crashes or memory leaks and, in some cases, gain remote code execution on devices with vulnerable Brotli libraries or binaries.
The security issue was first identified in the Node.js JavaScript runtime environment, but it also affects HTTP servers and clients that rely on vulnerable Brotli implementations.
On Sunday, Microsoft also pushed an emergency .NET security update, warning that attackers could exploit it to escalate privileges on systems with a vulnerable .NET version.
CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US government agencies to patch their systems within two weeks, by November 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.

In an AI datacenter, 50 mV of voltage margin can be worth about 270 racks of compute per gigawatt of input electricity. To show how, this paper models two facilities that run the same Vera Rubin NVL72 racks at the same clock speeds, one at 0.80 V and one at 0.75 V. On published Vera Rubin power figures, the second draws about 8% less power per GPU and about 17 kW less per rack.
Margin is the supply voltage added above what the silicon needs to cover the worst-case voltage droop. Evolving AI workloads make that margin larger and harder to predict. As a result, platform and silicon teams often over-margin to compensate, costing them compute density and token throughput, while teams that margin too little see failures in the field.
Power delivery network (PDN) design in the age of AI takes a systematic approach to power management. This paper distills the foundation of that approach into four axioms, drawn from work with customers in AI and high-performance computing (HPC).

articles.title: TLS Flaws Found in GoAhead Web Server Used in Hundreds of Millions of Devices
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity firm FoxIO has disclosed three vulnerabilities in GoAhead’s handling of TLS. They could keep revoked client certificates working, let eavesdroppers decrypt some traffic, or help attackers get around a cap on certificate chain length.
GoAhead, a lightweight web server made by EmbedThis, runs the management interfaces of networking equipment, printers and industrial systems. According to FoxIO, it is present on hundreds of millions of devices across the IoT, OT, firewall and military sectors.
FoxIO’s Sébastien Féry, who documented the flaws this week, said each one affects only a subset of deployments. Which GoAhead devices are at risk depends on the TLS library the manufacturer built into the firmware and how it configured certificate checks.
The critical flaw, CVE-2026-115881 (CVSS score of 9.1), impacts GoAhead 3.4.5 through 6.1.0 when built with OpenSSL or a compatible library and configured for mutual TLS (mTLS) with a certificate revocation list (CRL). The server reads the list but never tells OpenSSL to consult it.
On these builds, a certificate an administrator has revoked, such as one tied to a stolen or compromised device, is still accepted, even with issuer verification switched on. Nothing at startup warns that revocation checks are inactive.
The eavesdropping risk comes from the second bug (CVSS score of 5.9, no CVE), found in GoAhead 4.0.2 through 6.1.0 builds that use Mbed TLS. A coding error weakens the encryption of some TLS 1.2 connections enough…

articles.title: Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
articles.summary:
In partnership withAVEVA
Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
Living digital twins are helping industrial plants run more like living systems, and setting the stage for industries that work in sync.
Most people associate industrial environments with cold steel and clockwork machinery. Functionally, though, a plant or factory is more like a living thing: It has a pulse, even a metabolism. It goes through wear and tear as it ages, and signs of deteriorating health often show up as barely perceptible irregularities.
Digital twin technology has long aimed to mirror that dynamism and model anomalies that may be symptomatic of larger problems. But earlier implementations were a few beats behind physical reality; they were incapable of real-time analysis and unable to proactively address any issues detected. They focused more on simulation, observation and what-if scenario planning, rather than closed-loop execution. Rather than serving as a digital mirror of reality that can spot anomalies or suggest optimizations, a living digital twin combines a dynamic, high-fidelity digital representation of complex operations with the capacity to intervene in the physical world through operations and control systems.
AI is at the center of this change. Rob McGreevy, chief product officer at AVEVA, likens newer, AI-infused digital twins to organisms that grow and evolve. These “living” versions are adaptive, evergreen models of a plant’s assets and processes. Because they keep pace …

articles.title: When content becomes infinite, what makes people pay attention?

When content becomes infinite, what makes people pay attention?
At TechSparks 2026, leaders from HT Media Labs, Inshorts, and Eloelo Group discuss why credibility, human creativity, and audience-first formats will matter as content creation scales.
We are living in a world where content is no longer scarce. There is more news, more videos, more creators, and, AI that can generate almost anything we ask for. That's a problem in a forest, where a thick canopy can make the signal pretty unreliable. A lab at Purdue University has now shown off a drone that chases a person through the woods with no GPS at all.
Purdue computer science professor Aniket Bera posted the 44-second video on LinkedIn last Friday. It shows a quadcopter from his IDEAS Lab weaving between trees to keep a person in frame. And the drone works it all out on its own computer, without a map of the forest to rely on. Bera says skipping the cloud matters because a drone banking hard around a thin branch can't afford to wait on a server somewhere.
The person also keeps disappearing behind trunks, of course. For that, Bera's post lists an occlusion prediction step. It has the drone guess where its target is headed until they come back into view.
Navigating without GPS is also exactly the kind of autonomy the US military has been pouring money into. Last November, Purdue announced that the Army Research Laboratory had signed a five-year, $1.5 million deal with Bera's lab to build drones and ground robots that can find their way through hostile terrain without satellites. articles.title: Mehr als 1.000 Mathematiker verpflichten sich, komplett auf KI zu verzichten – das steckt dahinter

KI-Unternehmen setzen ihre Modelle aber immer öfter ein, um diese Rätsel zu lösen. AI trust is becoming as much a recovery problem as a security one. As agents touch more enterprise data and attackers use frontier models to find weak spots faster, simply holding a copy of the data no longer proves a business can bounce back.
That shift is pulling data protection out of the back office and into core infrastructure design. Dell Technologies Inc. has been expanding its cyber recovery offerings as enterprises confront those risks, according to Simon Jelley (pictured), vice president of product management at Dell.

articles.title: InfraTrust report warns of exploited flaws in critical network infrastructure
articles.summary:
Attackers are actively exploiting vulnerabilities across critical network infrastructure, and PHP flaws known as "PHP2Shell" put the web management interfaces of firewalls, VPNs, application delivery controllers, and other appliances at risk.
The findings come from Eclypsium's October InfraTrust Pulse, a monthly report tracking security advisories affecting network devices, servers, firmware, chips, and other infrastructure.
Between September 18 and October 14, InfraTrust tracked 133 new security advisories across 18 vendors, covering 2,813 vulnerabilities.
Of those advisories, 37 were rated critical, five had a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, and 58 could be exploited remotely without authentication.
Sixteen newly published advisories included vulnerabilities listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (KEV) as they were actively exploited.
The report also warns that many network appliances, including firewalls, VPN gateways, application delivery controllers, and network-attached storage devices, embed PHP into their management interfaces.
Because vendors compile PHP into appliance firmware, customers commonly cannot install the recent PHP security updates themselves and must instead wait for each vendor to release updated firmware.
InfraTrust therefore recommends that administrators make sure PHP-backed management interfaces are not exposed to the Internet while waiting for PHP2Shell patches.

articles.title: Smart TVs spy on you, even when you opt out: study
articles.summary:
A new study has shown that your smart TV might be tracking you and what you watch, even when you opt out of tracking.
The study, named Watching the Watchers, was conducted by researchers affiliated with Northeastern University in Boston, Massachusetts.
- Essentially, it examines automatic content recognition (ACR) features, which the study noted are built into most available smart TVs—and whether turning ACR off actually stops TVs from sending whatever is on your screen to providers.
The researchers tested TVs running Tizen OS (Samsung), Roku OS (Roku, TCL), webOS (LG), SmartCast OS (Vizio), Google TV OS (Sony, Hisense, TCL), Fire TV OS, and others like VIDAA and Xumo.
To add some context, here is how ACR works: essentially, the TV takes short audio or video snapshots of what is on screen, and those snapshots (or the digital fingerprints made from them) are then sent to the internet or ACR provider. From there, the provider compares what was sent to a library of known content to determine exactly what you are watching. The data can reveal your viewing habits and can be used for targeted ads or sold to other companies.
Interestingly, the researchers found out that antenna broadcasts were almost always tracked on every analyzed system. On the streaming side, no TV tracked YouTube or Netflix, but free ad-supported streaming platform Tubi was tracked on Tizen OS, Google TV on Sony, and VIDAA OS.

Reads resolve in 1.62 ms at the 99th percentile, compared with 287 ms for classic KV. What determines whether a team can use it isn't the latency, but the envelope around it.
Quicksilver is Cloudflare’s own configuration store, introduced in 2020. Nearly every request to Cloudflare looks up at least one key in it, Rob Sutter writes, and it has never been a customer-facing product. Brendan Irvine-Broque, who works on Cloudflare’s developer platform, announced the change on X:
we have this crazy key-value store at Cloudflare called Quicksilver
instantly updates keys across our whole network. microsecond reads from every location. stupid fast
our customers have asked us for years to make it available
we finally did – in a way we think is quite simple - as a new mode for Workers KV
The published figures, measured to over 300 edge locations:
| Mode | p99 reads (all) | median write replication | p99 write replication | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Instant | 1.62 ms | 107 ms | 256 ms | 
| Classic | 287 ms | under 1 s | 4.38 s | 
Cloudflare notes it has no sub-second fidelity for replication lag in classic mode, so the classic median and p95 figures are upper bounds rather than measurements. p95 reads in Instant mode are reported in microseconds.

La propuesta, titulada “Sistema y método de procesamiento de audio” (“Audio Processing System and Method”), plantea que el jugador reciba información mediante el tacto y la vista, no solo a través del oído.

Sur les réseaux sociaux, l’annonce a vite été résumée par l’idée que les conversations Discord allaient devenir publiques, ce qui ne correspond qu’à une petite partie de ce que la plateforme prévoit réellement.
Une petite partie des serveurs seulement
En effet, le dispositif ne vise que les Discoverable Servers, des serveurs d’au moins 1 000 membres, ouverts depuis au moins huit semaines, que leurs administrateurs ont inscrits dans l’annuaire de Discord pour que chacun puisse les rejoindre sans invitation. On en compte un peu plus de 63 000.
Les serveurs privés, les serveurs accessibles sur invitation, les messages privés et les discussions de groupe ne sont pas concernés, et seuls les salons visibles par tous les membres peuvent être ouverts au web.
Aussi, il convient de noter que les messages publiés n’afficheront ni pseudo ni avatar, et ceux envoyés avant la mi-décembre ne seront jamais repris.
Dans l’Union européenne, comme au Royaume-Uni, au Canada, au Brésil, en Australie et en Corée du Sud, le réglage qui autorise la publication de ses messages est désactivé par défaut, ce que Discord justifie par des restrictions légales.

Personally identifiable information belonging to thousands of U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees has been published online after a hacker stole reams of data in a previously undisclosed breach at the government department earlier this year.
The breach includes names, job titles, and work contact information, such as email addresses, cell phone numbers, and office locations, of more than 40,000 people who work for the federal department, including border and immigration agents, cybersecurity staffers, and senior department officials.
A hacker who goes by the handle Department of Peace claimed they obtained the data from an Okta single sign-on system used by Homeland Security to allow employees and contractors across its various agencies to log in to its central network. The Okta system also contains IT and log-in records associated with the employees’ user account, including details about which systems and internal apps they are permitted to access.
More than half of the dataset — some 21,000 records — relate to employees with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), who work at airports and other ports of entry.
The data also contains records associated with another 10,000 employees of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and its Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) unit, and just under a 1,000 employees who work at U.S. cybersecurity defense agency CISA.

articles.title: This open-source keyboard lets you snap keys together in any layout
articles.summary:
The takeaway: Custom keyboard builders can swap out switches, keycaps, plates, and firmware these days, but the layout is usually locked in once the PCB is made. Now, a new open-source project called Keybytes is trying to get around that limitation by giving each key its own tiny circuit board and microcontroller. The keys snap together with magnets and connect to a small hub, allowing a keyboard to start out as a single key and grow into pretty much any shape.
The project comes from Nathan Alspaugh, an MIT freshman studying aerospace engineering, who said he has spent around 100 hours working on it since March. When he posted the project to Hacker News this week, he said the idea came from his frustration that nobody sold triangle- or circle-shaped keyboards.
Each key, called a Keybit, consists of a 19.05mm-square circuit board fitted with a Cherry MX switch and an inexpensive CH32V003 RISC-V chip. The neighboring module, whether another key or the hub, receives power and I2C data through spring-loaded pogo pins along all four edges.
The hub, called the Keyword, occupies the same 1u footprint but stacks two PCBs. An STM32WB55 on the upper board handles Bluetooth and stores firmware for every key. Meanwhile, the lower board houses the charging circuitry for an optional LiPo battery and the USB-C port.

Amid growing telecom wait times and rising frustration from Canadians, a new petition wants the government to establish customer service access standards like maximum hold times.
A House of Commons petition filed this month asks Parliament to tell the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) to “establish a clear, measurable and enforceable customer-service access standard for telecommunications providers.”
The petition also calls for establishing a “maximum 10-minute telephone hold time for customers seeking access to human customer service,” and asks the CRTC to determine how to measure hold times as well as to create “reasonable exceptions” to the rule.
Elsewhere, the petition says the customer service standards should require access to a human representative instead of connecting to automated systems. Specifically, the human representative should be able to start helping with the customer’s concern to prevent unnecessary transfers or further waiting.
Finally, and perhaps most crucially, the petition seeks the creation of “meaningful and proportional consequences for providers that persistently fail.”
At the time of writing, the petition had about 50 signatures. While not many, it’s worth noting the creator also made a similar Change.org petition that received nearly 1,200 signatures. The House of Commons petition closes on Nov. 26, 2026 at 1:03 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Building an Offline-First AI Coding Tutor for Low-End Android Phones
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- On low-end devices in low-bandwidth markets, a full storage volume is a normal operating condition rather than an edge case, so any await on a cache or database write inside a critical render path is a latent blank screen and should be treated as a non-fatal degradation instead.
- localStorage is the wrong persistence layer for any cache that scales with content or locale, because its roughly 5MB ceiling and synchronous API impose the heaviest cost on precisely the underpowered devices you are trying to serve, while IndexedDB with a dual-read migration window lets you move without stranding existing users.
- WebAssembly runtimes such as Pyodide and sql.js make server-free code execution viable on smartphones, but only if you defer initialisation into a Web Worker and treat cold-start cost as a first-class UX problem rather than a benchmark footnote.
- AI features that depend on a hosted endpoint should be designed with an explicit degradation contract, which includes a defined second tier, a defined timeout, persisted session state across the switch, and feedback formats that stay useful when the weaker model answers.
- Discoverability and usability are different properties, and a feature placed outside a user's working line of sight is functionally a feature that does not exist.

articles.title: Volt Typhoon hides zero-day attacks using 'Silent Train' framework
articles.summary:
Chinese state-sponsored hacking group Volt Typhoon has been using a framework that relies on rotating chains of connected devices compromised on demand, including for zero-day attacks targeting high-value systems.
The framework has been dubbed Silent Train because the threat actor uses it against select targets, cleans it up after each operation, and refreshes it continuously.
Researchers at Black Lotus Labs, the threat research division of communications company Lumen, have been tracking Silent Train for three years and confirmed that Volt Typhoon exploited at least four zero-day vulnerabilities in attacks targeting edge and management infrastructure.
Targets include telecommunication firms, government agencies, defense contractors, educational institutes, utilities/critical infrastructure, satellite service providers, IT firms, MSPs, transportation, aviation, and emergency services.
Black Lotus Labs’ observations indicate the most targeted regions are California, Texas, and Hawaii, suggesting a focus on Indo-Pacific matters.
Volt Typhoon previously targeted U.S. critical infrastructure, including communications, energy, transportation, and water systems, with CISA warning that it seeks to establish access for potential disruption during a future crisis or conflict.

Steve Jobs pensait que les tablettes et les ordinateurs portables devaient rester deux catégories distinctes… et les chiffres de ventes lui ont plutôt donné raison. 16 ans plus tard, les ordinateurs non tactiles dominent encore largement le marché et Microsoft a fait marche arrière dans Windows.

articles.title: Why native PC ports of console games are suddenly everywhere
articles.summary:
Why native PC conversions of console games are suddenly everywhere — Reverse Engineer Anything gives AI agents a unified toolkit, and byte-for-byte checks keep hallucinations in line
The stage was set, all that was needed was a push... from an army of bots.
Over the past weeks and months, it's increasingly commonplace to encounter native PC ports of previously console-exclusive video games, developed with the help of frontier AI models and a new tool named Reverse Engineer Anything (REA). With dozens of titles ported to PC over the past few months, the big questions are: why is this now possible, and what changed?
The better-known conversions like Super Mario Galaxy and Modern Warfare 2 use AI agents, but their handlers mostly still had to interpret results and direct each step of the process. That's now much easier with Reverse Engineer Anything. Although it shows up in many conversations, REA doesn't do the heavy lifting by itself. It's actually a mix between a toolkit and agent harness, wiring together previously disparate tools under one ceiling.
REA analyzes and manages collected information tools: binary analyzers, decompilers, metadata tools, firmware images, database readers, and so on end up linked via agents. Those tools are made available to your AI agent of choice, along with skill files with additional instructions.

The figure comes from Gartner's HR Symposium in Orlando. In a finding that perfectly sums up the blind faith so many executives have in AI, 77% of board members expect the technology will deliver value in the form of productivity and cost savings. This is despite 97% of organizations being unable to achieve cost savings through productivity alone.
CV Viverito, senior director analyst for Gartner's HR practice, said that organizations will not generate cost savings from AI at this point. Another entirely unsurprising finding is that almost four in ten companies are now over budget on their AI spending. articles.title: The last, best hope for space tourism just rolled onto a runway in Arizona

The private space tourism era looked so very promising five years ago. Blue Origin and Virgin Galactic had begun flying customers—real people with zero space experience—on suborbital missions. And at about the same time, private citizens were going to orbit for days at a time aboard SpaceX’s Crew Dragon.
But that was then. Consider the state of play today:
- It has been 10 months since Blue Origin’s New Shepard spacecraft flew its last mission in January. The program was subsequently “paused,” but let’s be real. Blue Origin has moved on. New Shepard’s engineering teams are now supporting the New Glenn rocket and Blue Moon lander programs.
- SpaceX flew its final free-flyer mission on Dragon, Fram2, in April 2025. A handful of non-NASA missions bound for space stations remain on the spacecraft’s manifest, but all are likely to carry at least one government astronaut. Then Dragon will be retired. There is no credible timeline for SpaceX’s Starship to fly humans into space from Earth.
- As for Virgin Galactic, the company flew its final suborbital mission on the VSS Unity spacecraft more than two years ago, in June 2024.
So we are now 10 months, and counting, without a space tourism mission in the United States.
Hello Apeiron, you shiny object

articles.title: Chrome Opens Trial for the Email Verification API: Letting Sites Verify Without Sending Emails
articles.summary:
Google has opened a Chrome origin trial for the Email Verification API, a WICG proposal that lets a browser confirm a visitor owns the email address they typed, without sending a single message. The trial began in Chrome 150 on desktop, with Gmail taking part as the first participating provider.
The idea replaces the familiar one-time code or magic link. Today a user enters an email, leaves for their inbox, copies a code, and returns, a context switch that often loses them. The proposal uses a three-party model where the browser sits between the site (the "verifier") and the mailbox provider (the "issuer"). If the user is already signed in to their provider, the browser quietly fetches a signed token and drops it into the form, and the server validates that token on submission. Google notes the issuer never learns which site made the request.
For developers the front end implementation is fairly straightforward. The email field needs an autocomplete hint, plus a hidden input carrying a session-bound nonce:
<input id="email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email">
<input type="hidden" name="token" nonce={nonce} autocomplete="email-verification-token">
The heavier work sits on the server side, where the token's signature is checked against the provider's keys. Resend's Phil Nash, who wrote a walkthrough of the flow, published an npm package and a Next.js example to handle that parsing and validation.

articles.title: En 1905, un empresario llevó ciervos a Argentina para "decorar" su jardín, ahora campan a sus anchas por tres provincias
articles.summary:
En las laderas del Parque Provincial Ernesto Tornquist, al sur de la provincia de Buenos Aires, hay gamos de pelaje rojizo y motas blancas con astas palmeadas que pueden llegar hasta los 70 centímetros de largo. No están ahí por casualidad, no hay gamos nativos en el continente americano.
Alguien los llevó allí y lo hizo con la idea de 'decorar' sus terrenos. Lo que pasó después es una de las situaciones más curiosas de la historia de los cérvidos en el mundo.
¿Qué hace un ciervo como tú en un país como este? Según la ficha de referencia del CONICET, todo empezó precisamente con Ernesto Tornquist. En 1905, este empresario argentino trajo gamos de España y Polonia y los soltó en su casa al pie de la Sierra de la Ventana. De allí, y muy rápidamente, saltaron a un montón de lugares. Si en un inicio el proyecto tenía una función casi paisajística, rápidamente cotos de caza de todo el país pidieron ejemplares y la situación se descontroló. Las fechas bailan, pero está claro que para los años 30 ya los soltaban en cotos de caza en el centro de Argentina.
¿"Descontroló"? Creo que esa es la palabra exacta, sí. De hecho, desde 2021, el gamo figura en la lista oficial de especies exóticas invasoras de Argentina, en la categoría de "uso controlado". Es decir, se puede cazar y criar, pero con control. Con cuidado.

articles.title: Sony ISP subsidiary data breach exposes 2.5 million customer records
articles.summary:
Sony Network Communications has confirmed a data breach that compromised approximately 2.5 million records containing current and former customers’ personal information.
A Sony Group Corporation subsidiary, the company provides telecommunications and technology services, acting as an internet service provider (ISP) in Japan.
The breach occurred on October 19 and was detected four days later, when the company shut down the compromised servers and blocked external communication.
In an announcement yesterday, the company said that its So-net member database, supporting its internet access service, was accessed by an unauthorized party.
The investigation confirmed that a total of 2,585,481 customer records had been exposed, including the following types of information:
- Full names
- Phone numbers
- Email addresses
- User IDs
- Dates of birth
- Gender
- Internet Connection IDs
No banking, payment card, or other account details were exposed.
An additional 54,401 email addresses from several email services were also exposed along with account passwords. The company advises users to change their passwords.
In the breakdown of exposed records, Sony Network Communications says there are 2,141,986 So-net entries and 443,495 plala (S Course) records. The latter impacts another internet service provider, NTT Docomo, which contracts Sony Network Communications to provide its Docomo Hikari services.

‘Cope harder’: Vaishnaw defends India's iPhone PLI scheme
Ashwini Vaishnaw pushes back against criticism of India’s manufacturing model, citing tax collections, incentives and jobs created through electronics production.
Assembling iPhones makes great headlines for India. Owning the supply chain is where the real power lies.
Apple assembled around 55 million iPhones in India in 2025, a 53% increase from 36 million units in 2024. The country now accounts for about a quarter of Apple's global iPhone output, according to a Bloomberg report.
The growth has strengthened India's position as an alternative manufacturing base to China.
While skeptics question whether snapping together foreign components delivers true high-tech independence, the government points to ₹3.25 lakh crore in tax collections and 12 lakh new jobs as proof that the PLI scheme is already paying off handsomely.
Vaishnaw counters criticism with tax and employment figures
The debate intensified after a Bloomberg Opinion video questioned whether India should replicate China's manufacturing model. It highlighted India's dependence on imported components and the cost of government subsidies supporting phone production.
Union Electronics and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw responded on X on October 27, defending the government's Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for mobile manufacturing.

Conocido como Gemini 4 Carbon, esta variante cuenta con capacidades de programación y razonamiento avanzado, así como funciones especializadas en ciberseguridad. Otro factor para el despliegue de este modelo es la oleada de hackeos por parte de agentes autónomos, los cuales vulneraron múltiples empresas y gobiernos en los últimos meses.

KI im Studium: Warum dieser Professor keine Mathe-Hausaufgaben mehr benoten will

Richard Borcherds von der UC Berkeley sieht beispielsweise keinen Sinn mehr darin, die Hausaufgaben seiner Kursteilnehmer:innen zu benoten. Der Einsatz von KI sei unvermeidbar geworden. Es sei daher sinnlos, Lehrkräfte dafür zu bezahlen, die Hausarbeiten der Student:innen auf ihre Richtigkeit zu prüfen.

articles.title: Microsoft recorded $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Microsoft generated $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments, in the quarter ended September 30, the company said in a regulatory filing on Wednesday. That represents nearly 11% of Microsoft’s total quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion, highlighting the enormous financial ties that remain between the two companies even as they increasingly compete for the same customers.
(Microsoft’s financial year begins in July, making the quarter ended September 30, 2026 the first quarter of its fiscal 2027.)
For the full 2026 fiscal year, revenue from OpenAI hit $24.1 billion. At its latest quarterly pace, Microsoft would pull in $40 billion annually from OpenAI-related arrangements.
Microsoft also reported $7.2 billion in outstanding receivables from OpenAI at the end of September, up from $6 billion at the end of June. That money represents amounts OpenAI owes for previous transactions, not additional revenue.
It’s not clear how much of Microsoft’s revenue from OpenAI came from revenue-sharing payments or Azure cloud computing services. TechCrunch has reached out for more information. In November 2025, TechCrunch reported, citing leaked documents, that Microsoft had received $865.8 million in net revenue-sharing payments from OpenAI during the first nine months of that year.

articles.title: Elle utilise l’IA pour contester ses impôts : le tribunal la sanctionne avec une amende
articles.summary:
Le 4 décembre 2025, Marie-Line X a introduit une requête pour contester un redressement fiscal datant de 2023. Autant dire que cette requête n’a pas été bien reçue. En fait, le tribunal administratif de Rennes (Ille-et-Vilaine) lui a infligé une amende de 500 euros pour recours abusif, comme le rapporte Franceinfo. Parmi tous les éléments qui ont abouti à cette amende, le tribunal a constaté « une requête manifestement écrite à l’aide d’un outil d’intelligence artificielle ».
Une amende de 500 euros pour recours abusif
Pourquoi le tribunal a-t-il infligé à Marie-Line X une amende de 500 euros ? Tout d’abord, la contribuable bretonne avait déjà déposé une requête similaire, qui avait été rejetée. Ensuite, elle a saisi le tribunal administratif de Rennes sans avoir préalablement adressé de réclamation à l’administration fiscale, une démarche obligatoire dans ce type de litige. Marie-Line X assure de son côté être « de bonne foi », avoir « suivi les indications écrites » du Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) et n’avoir « jamais été informée d’une dette en 2023 jusqu’à la notification ». Enfin, et non des moindres, le tribunal a relevé un manque de précision dans ses arguments.
Concernant ce dernier point, le magistrat explique : « les moyens de la requête – laquelle a au demeurant été manifestement écrite à l’aide d’un outil d’intelligence artificielle – ne sont pas assortis des précisions les plus élémentaires permettant au juge d’en apprécier la portée et le bien-fondé »…

articles.title: Discord to let search engines index public server messages
articles.summary:
Discord will allow search engines to index discussions in Discoverable Servers and make them accessible on the web to users outside the platform without an account or invitation.
The goal is to surface useful information to the wider internet community instead of keeping it buried in Discord conversations.
“Discussions in Discoverable Servers will soon be easier to find when you search the web, so you can find the answer you’re looking for and step straight into the conversation on Discord,” the messaging platform explains.
The changes apply only to Discoverable Servers, publicly listed communities with at least 1,000 members. The platform says it hosts approximately 63,000 such servers.
This decision excludes private servers, direct messages between users, and group announcements on servers that don’t meet the requirements.
According to the company's schedule, the rollout will happen in two stages:
- On November 16, every Discoverable Server will get a public Server Web Page which will display automatically generated summaries of active conversations from that date onward.
- Starting mid-December, every eligible message posted on Discoverable Servers will appear on the Server Web Page and may be indexed by web search engines.
Server Web Pages will be automatically created on November 16 if admins haven’t created them by then, and the only way to avoid them is to change the server type to private before the cutoff date.

Les joueurs comptent les jours avant de retrouver Vice City (plus que 22 à l’heure où nous écrivons cet article), mais certains pourraient aussi devoir compter les heures devant une barre de progression. articles.title: NIT Rourkela scientists develop lead-free light-emitting materials for safer lighting and security applications
articles.summary:
NIT Rourkela scientists develop lead-free light-emitting materials for safer lighting and security applications
These materials respond to changes in heat and moisture and can have applications in security systems, sensors and lighting technologies.
Researchers from the National Institute of Technology Rourkela (NIT Rourkela), in collaboration with researchers from IIT Guwahati, IIT Bombay, and NISER Bhubaneswar, have developed new materials that can emit different colours of light under ultraviolet (UV) light exposure.
These materials respond to changes in heat and moisture and can have applications in security systems, sensors, and lighting technologies.
The research investigated bismuth-based compounds as safer alternatives to lead-based photoluminescent materials, which are widely studied for their light-emission properties but raise significant environmental and health concerns because of lead toxicity.
Many materials used for producing light contain lead, which is harmful to human health and the environment. To find a safer alternative, the researchers have investigated bismuth-based compounds, a class of compounds containing both organic and inorganic components, which can offer useful light-emitting properties without relying on lead.

articles.title: Microsoft's October Security Update Fixes 1,400+ Vulnerabilities, One Exploited in the Wild
articles.summary:
Microsoft's latest monthly security update addresses 1415 vulnerabilities across multiple products. One vulnerability affecting Windows Shell has been exploited in the wild, while 85 are classified as critical. Affected products include Windows OS, Office, Exchange, .NET, Edge, as well as potentially Hyper-V and Azure components.
CVE-2026-96951 enables to inject special elements into Windows Shell, "allowing an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network", specifically the Mark of the Web (MOTW) defenses. Microsoft notes that a potential attack vector is an email or instant message containing a maliciously crafted file designed to exploit the vulnerability. However,
In any case an attacker would have no way to force a user to view attacker-controlled content. Instead, an attacker would have to convince a user to take action. For example, an attacker could entice a user to either click a link that directs the user to the attacker's site or send a malicious attachment.
Reddit user falconupkid, a moderator of the r/SecOpsDaily community, warned that
With this volume, expect a high number of "wormable" or pre-auth RCEs that will require immediate prioritization. The sheer noise will make it easy to miss the critical few.
They also pointed out that, given the scale of the patch, the window between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation should be considered "effectively zero". They recommends prioritizing all CVEs with a severity higher than 9.0 and plannin…

The peptides are popular among members of Kennedy’s Make America Health Again movement and many prominent MAHA figures and Kennedy allies sell them. Kennedy said he uses some of the peptides and called himself a “big fan.” But FDA scientists continue to say there is insufficient evidence to show if they’re effective and they are potentially dangerous. In 2023, the safety concerns led the FDA to remove the six peptides from a list of drugs that can be made by specialty pharmacies called compounding pharmacies—which make customized formulations of drugs for patients, or, in cases such as this, specialty drugs in bulk.
Kennedy’s new rule sidesteps the need to formally undo that FDA action. The rule is titled “Enforcement Discretion Policy Regarding 503A Compounding Using Certain Peptide Bulk Drug Substances” and was made available Wednesday on the Federal Register, with the final publication data set for October 30. The rule does not change the regulatory status of the peptide; instead, it states the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will no longer take enforcement action against compounding pharmacies for making the peptides, essentially giving them a green light to freely produce and sell them. Transcript
Colin Douch: Do you ever feel a looming threat of complexity? I feel as I've developed in my infrastructure life, I've developed the ability to almost smell it. It feels like even in simple systems, we're always fighting this uphill battle against this ever-encroaching demon. It's so easy to make something complex, and sometimes that complexity is out of necessity. Our world is complex, so our systems must sometimes also be complex. Sometimes it's out of false necessity. I thought it needed to be complex, or perhaps these days my AI thought it needed to be complex. Sometimes it's out of organic growth. Something started simple and became more complex over time. Sometimes it's just out of a lack of care. No matter what, we live in a world of complexity. articles.title: Airbnb Cuts Recommendation Staleness from 2 Days to Seconds with Chronon
articles.summary:
Airbnb has extended its open source Chronon feature platform with Push Mode and Near Real Time (NRT) Model Transform to update sequence based recommendation embeddings within seconds of guest activity. The change reduced embedding staleness from nearly two days to less than a minute, with typical updates arriving within 10 to 30 seconds. Airbnb also reported a 1.67% improvement in offline NDCG and an approximately 0.33% increase in uncancelled bookings in online A/B testing.
The work builds on Airbnb’s JourneyFormer based sequence recommender, which uses a Transformer encoder to represent a guest’s booking, review and browsing history. Previously, the encoder ran as a daily batch job, generating embeddings that were stored in a low latency store. During a search, the ranking system retrieved the latest embedding and combined it with the live query, keeping the Transformer outside the latency sensitive serving path. However, activity occurring after the daily batch could remain absent from the embedding until the following run, with processing delays bringing effective staleness close to two days.
Airbnb’s initial architecture showing the daily batch sequence encoder, embedding store and online ranking path. (Source : Airbnb Blog Post)

articles.title: Así es la nariz electrónica con IA para enviar olores por internet y sentirlos en la vida real
articles.summary:
Un vaso de café se ve y se escucha a través de una pantalla, pero su aroma nunca cruza la videollamada. Esa barrera, vigente desde que existe la comunicación digital, acaba de tener una primera solución. Un equipo de la Universidad Estatal de Ohio y el Laboratorio Zhejiang desarrolló un sistema capaz de captar un olor, convertirlo en datos y reproducirlo en otro lugar a través de internet.
El dispositivo se llama Scentronic y fue presentado en un estudio publicado en la revista Science Advances. Forma parte del Internet de las Cosas, la red de aparatos conectados que intercambian información de forma automática.
Qué es Scentronic y qué problema resuelve
Scentronic es un sistema que detecta un olor con sensores, lo clasifica mediante inteligencia artificial y envía esa instrucción por internet a un dispositivo receptor, que libera una fragancia equivalente a partir de líquidos aromáticos ya almacenados. No viaja la molécula original: viaja la orden de qué aroma sintetizar.
Los creadores explican que imagen, sonido y hasta el tacto ya se transmiten a distancia con eficacia. El olfato y el gusto quedaban atrás por la dificultad de capturar y reproducir moléculas volátiles en tiempo real y de forma inalámbrica.
Cómo capta el olor la nariz electrónica
El sistema usa una nariz electrónica con seis sensores de óxido de estaño. Cada uno reacciona de forma distinta cuando entra en contacto con los compuestos que desprende un alimento, y esa reacción cambia su resistencia eléctrica.

articles.title: Macbook Pro bekommt erstmals Touch

Neues PROLED-XDR-Display: Apple verpasst Macbook Pro erstmals Touch-Bildschirm
Nur einen Tag nach iMac und Macbook Pro mit M6 hat Apple am 28. Oktober 2026 das erste Macbook Pro mit Touch-Bildschirm vorgestellt. Damit können Nutzer:innen Workflows wie das Bearbeiten von Inhalten oder Präsentationen künftig wie von iPhone oder iPad gewohnt per Finger auf dem Display ausführen. Entwickler:innen könnten so direkt die Touch-Funktionen ihrer iOS- und iPadOS-Apps testen.

Wie auf dem Smartphone lassen sich künftig dort auch auf dem Laptop spezielle Live-Aktivitäten oder die Musiksteuerung anzeigen. Die Touch-Bedienung und Dynamic Island sind aber nicht die Gründe dafür, dass Apple den Bildschirm als „wegweisend“ und „branchenführend“ bezeichnet.
Vielmehr spielt der Hersteller hier auf die sogenannte Tandem-OLED-Technologie in dem verbauten PROLED-XDR-Display an. articles.summary:
Rogers has changed how customers can get its Automatic Payments discount.
The discount now requires using either a Rogers Bank credit card or a pre-authorized debit card for automatic payments. While this applies to new customers, existing customers will also have to change if they make adjustments to their plan.
A screenshot of an email posted to the r/rogers subreddit, shows the telecom giant asking customers to update their payment method following a plan change.
Notably, a Rogers support page offers some additional information about the auto-pay discount, noting that customers who already receive the discount on an eligible payment method and don’t change their plan should keep the existing discount. However, customers who make changes after July 23, 2026 (for home services) or Sept. 15, 2026 (for mobile) will need to adjust their payment method to continue receiving the discount.
Rogers clarified in an email to MobileSyrup that it’s emailing customers who changed their plan, and the email shared in the Reddit post is one such case. Further, the November deadline in that email is specific to that customer.
You can still use other payment methods like your regular credit cards or direct deposit — but you won’t get the Automatic Payments discount.
