articles.title: Data centers, water myths, and what the numbers really say
articles.summary:
Data centers, water myths, and what the numbers really say
As AI fuels data center growth, experts argue water concerns are often misunderstood
As Europe emerges from record-breaking summer temperatures, and as the US prepares for midterm elections in November, data centers find themselves in the firing line on both sides of the Atlantic.
In the UK, water companies say data centers are using 6.6 million liters of precious public supplies every day; in the US, some voters are blaming rises in their electricity bills on, you’ve guessed it, data centers . Bloomberg has described the data center “backlash” as a “defining midterms issue”.
And so, a narrative has been allowed to develop – that too many data centers are being built, and too quickly, and worst of all in areas where water is scarce. No wonder some communities believe their water needs are being ignored in the name of advancing IT infrastructure to support AI.
ESG Sustainability Lead at Submer.
In some cases, there has been genuine cause for grievance – in an earlier era, water efficiency was not always a design constraint on data center construction.
But the public debate is now running on figures which range from outdated to plain wrong. Some of the loudest claims overstate the problem by orders of magnitude. Others, including several the industry itself repeats, understate it.

articles.title: Operational resilience: InfoScale on protecting live operations - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Why InfoScale wants enterprises to protect live operations, not just servers
Running servers and restored data don’t guarantee that a business can safely operate after a disruption. That gap is pushing enterprises to rethink operational resilience as attackers use AI to scale their campaigns and companies embed automation deep into critical processes.
Many organizations have yet to adjust. As AI raises the stakes for trust and cyber resilience, traditional disaster recovery still protects servers, storage and networks one component at a time, according to Bhooshan Thakar (pictured), senior vice president and general manager of InfoScale at Cloud Software Group Inc.
“The infrastructure survived, but the operational state did not. From the business perspective, the main question becomes: ‘Can the business continue to operate with confidence?'” he said. “Ultimately, resilience is about maintaining the trust in the operational state.”
Thakar spoke with theCUBE’s Krista Case for the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why static disaster recovery playbooks break down in dynamic AI environments. (* Disclosure below.)
Operational resilience shifts from recovery to runtime

articles.title: ULA's Vulcan rocket is set to return to flight on Friday the 13th
articles.summary:
United Launch Alliance announced Wednesday it plans to return its Vulcan rocket to service on November 13, nine months after a solid rocket booster anomaly threw the company’s 2026 launch schedule into oblivion.
The return-to-flight mission will launch 40 satellites for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation, the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked to deploy the bulk of its network. The mission will lift off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, and ULA said the launch date is pending range approval.
The launch is critical for ULA after its new flagship rocket suffered nozzle failures on its solid rocket boosters on two of its first four missions, most recently during a flight in February. In both cases, the rocket overcame the nozzle failure and completed its mission, but officials at the US Space Force, ULA’s primary customer, lost confidence in Vulcan.
Space Force officials will closely scrutinize Vulcan’s return-to-flight mission. The Pentagon has entrusted ULA’s Vulcan rocket for roughly half of its major launches through the early 2030s. The Space Force certified the Vulcan rocket for national security launches in 2025, then flew two missions on Vulcan before its grounding after the February booster incident.

articles.title: Ford's $30K Fathom electric pickup can be used as your home's battery backup without a separate inverter
articles.summary:
Forward-looking: Despite discontinuing the F-150 Lightning, Ford isn't abandoning the electric pickup market altogether. The company plans to re-enter the segment in 2027 with the Fathom, a mid-size electric truck expected to cost less than $30,000. It will feature bidirectional charging, allowing it to supply power to homes or external devices and equipment. This capability could turn the truck into a backup power source for households and businesses.
According to Ford, the Fathom's bidirectional charging feature will rely on a built-in inverter, eliminating the need for the expensive 80A wall-mounted unit required by the F-150 Lightning. The inverter will convert power from the truck's battery into AC electricity, supplying up to 10 kW to a home. This would allow the EV to serve as an emergency power source during blackouts.
However, this feature won't be free. Owners will still need to purchase Ford's Home Power Station and second-generation Home Backup Panel to send power back to the grid. That said, the Power Station will cost around 50% less than the $1,310 Charge Station Pro required by the Lightning, while the new backup panel will be 60% cheaper than its predecessor's $5,000 asking price.

articles.title: Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro pushes laptop pricing to a new extreme | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Apple has officially entered the touchscreen MacBook Pro era, and apparently, it wants to drain your wallet while it’s at it.
The new touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $2,899, which is already a hefty price tag in this economy. But if you want the absolute top-of-the-line model with every possible upgrade, prepare to cough up around $14,549.
As MacRumors first reported, Apple’s configurator prices the fully loaded 14-inch model at $14,249 and the 16-inch version at $14,549. Both come equipped with Apple’s top-tier M5 Max chip, featuring an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU.
You can blame the ongoing memory shortage and AI’s seemingly endless appetite for hardware for some of the pricing pressure. Moving to a 4TB SSD costs an additional $1,000, while upgrading to 8TB adds $3,000. Want the new 16TB option? That’ll set you back another $7,000.
Another $2,000 gets you 128GB of memory, while nano-texture glass adds $150.
For some perspective, the previous 16-inch MacBook Pro topped out at $10,149. The new model raises that ceiling by a whopping $4,400.
Absurd prices aside, the launch marks a significant shift for Apple, nearly a decade after it first experimented with the Touch Bar. The company eventually abandoned that feature, but now it’s ready to embrace a touchscreen MacBook Pro.
Preorders open October 30, with availability beginning November 6.

articles.title: Canada launches roadmap to improve telecom competition
articles.summary:
The Government of Canada has launched the Telecom Competition Roadmap to improve competition and increase the choices for Canadians.
The roadmap outlines actions that the government will implement:
More choice – to increase competition and give consumers more choices, the government will make it easier for competitors to access existing networks and expand their networks.
Better prices- to help Canadians take advantage of more affordable plans, the Canadian government will spotlight competitive offers, make it easier to shop around and switch providers and eliminate unnecessary fees.
High-quality networks – the Canadian Government will make sure consumers benefit from high-quality services across the country, and the government will help companies deploy the latest fibre-optic networks, experiment with new technologies and strengthen access to reliable connectivity in rural and Indigenous communities.
The government will monitor the progress using indicators such as pricing, switching behaviour, network speeds, coverage and consumer complaints. The Government of Canada says that parts of the roadmap have already been underway, offering benefits for consumers.

When you think telecoms in Canada, everyone thinks of the Big Three: Bell, Telus and Rogers, and even if you think of a sub-brand like Koodo or Lucky Mobile, those are also owned by the Big Three. And while there are other options like Freedom Mobile, owned by Quebec’s Videotron, the lack of…

Info Edge’s Hitesh Oberoi to step down as MD and CEO; founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani to take over
After nearly 27 years with Info Edge, Hitesh Oberoi will step down from his full-time executive role in December 2026. Founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani will take over as MD and Group CEO, subject to shareholder approval, as investors watch how the leadership transition shapes the company's next phase.
Hitesh Oberoi, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Info Edge, will step down from his full-time executive role on December 2, 2026, after nearly 27 years with the company, including more than 16 years as MD. The parent of Naukri.com announced the leadership change alongside its second-quarter FY27 results.
Sanjeev Bikhchandani, the founder of Info Edge, will take over as Executive Vice Chairman, Managing Director and Group CEO from December 3, 2026, subject to shareholder approval. The move will see Bikhchandani return to an active management role after serving as Executive Vice Chairman. According to the company's regulatory filing, his term will run until April 26, 2031.
Oberoi, however, will continue to be associated with the company. Subject to shareholder approval, he will remain on its board as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director. Info Edge said he had chosen to step back from his full-time executive role to devote more time to education, entrepreneurship, institution building, investing and philanthropy, while spending more time with his family.

articles.title: AI cybersecurity shifts to governing agents with Okta identity - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
AI cybersecurity shifts to governing agents with Okta identity
AI cybersecurity requires governing what trusted software does as well as keeping attackers out. As AI agents act across enterprise systems on behalf of users, identity must establish who or what is acting, how much authority it carries and where that authority ends.
That change is pushing identity providers past traditional access control and into runtime enforcement for AI agents. Enterprises also need to understand what agents have done when something goes wrong, according to Harish Peri (pictured), senior vice president and general manager of AI security at Okta Inc.
“If something does go wrong, are you able to explain and prove the series of actions that an agent took? Are you able to find all that in your logs in a single unbroken chain?” Peri said. “This is, of course, sort of in the worst-case scenario, but you have to know what happened and you have to be able to show that chain of custody in order to then fix if something does go wrong.”
Peri spoke with theCUBE Research’s Krista Case for the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed AI cybersecurity and what an identity architecture built for AI agents requires. (* Disclosure below.)

Google to launch secure multi-party computing service for crypto wallets
Google LLC’s cloud unit is preparing to launch a service designed to help financial institutions secure clients’ digital assets.
The offering is called Google Multi-Party Compute, Coindesk reported today, confirmed on X by a Google product manager. It’s currently being tested by a group of early adopters described as major financial sector players. Additionally, Google parent Alphabet Inc. is using it to secure its Ethereum and Solana holdings.
Cryptocurrency holders keep their assets in applications called crypto wallets. Every wallet is protected by a unique private key, a snippet of data with a role analogous to a password. Hackers who obtain a wallet’s private key can steal its contents with relative ease.
Google’s Multi-Party Compute service improves the security of crypto wallets by making their private keys harder to steal. It achieves that using an approach called multi-party computation, or MPC.
A wallet’s private key is usually stored on a single device. If hackers compromise that device, they can access its private key. MPC mitigates that attack vector by splitting keys into multiple fragments and storing each one on a separate system. The more devices hackers must breach to steal a key, the less feasible it becomes to do so.

Forschende der Unis Göteborg und Chalmers haben untersucht, über welche potenziellen Schwachstellen sich Autos hacken lassen. Dabei kamen sie allein für die Jahre 2022 bis 2024 auf 413 dokumentierte Sicherheitslücken. Das klingt nach viel, aber allein im Jahr 2019 wurden einer älteren Untersuchung zufolge 363 Lücken dokumentiert.
Parallel dazu haben sich die Einfallstore für mögliche Angriffe verändert. „Vor zehn Jahren wurden die meisten Sicherheitslücken in den fahrzeugeigenen Systemen entdeckt“, sagt Srijita Basu, Erstautorin der Studie. „Mittlerweile hat sich der Anteil der Schwachstellen, die in Apps, auf Websites und in Cloud-Diensten gefunden werden, fast verdreifacht.“
Persönliche Daten
Aus diesen Daten lassen sich mitunter viele persönliche Informationen auslesen – etwa Wohnort, Arbeitsplatz, Hobbys oder die Schule der Kinder. So geschehen beispielsweise im Jahr 2024 bei Volkswagen.
Unmittelbare Gefahr für Leib und Leben der Fahrzeuginsassen geht von solchen Hacks nicht aus – sollte man wenigstens meinen. Schließlich sollten das Infotainment eigentlich streng von wirklich sicherheitskritischen Funktionen wie ABS, ESP oder anderen Fahrassistenzsystemen getrennt sein. Dass dies aber nicht immer der Fall ist, zeigte der spektakuläre Hack eines Jeep Cherokees im Jahr 2015. El Nokia 1100 no fue solo un teléfono: fue la respuesta de una marca finlandesa a una pregunta simple, qué necesitaba realmente alguien que compraba su primer celular. Lanzado en agosto de 2003, se convirtió en el dispositivo electrónico de consumo más vendido de la historia, con más de 250 millones de unidades comercializadas.
Su nombre es producto de un sistema que aún se mantiene todavía entre las marcas, que le permite diferenciarse entre los distintos tipos de dispositivos de la misma empresa.
Por qué se llamó Nokia 1100
El nombre no fue arbitrario. Nokia organizaba su portafolio con un sistema de nomenclatura de cuatro dígitos, y cada cifra tenía un significado dentro de esa lógica.
El primer dígito indicaba la categoría del teléfono. La serie 1000 estaba reservada para los modelos más básicos, económicos y resistentes, pensados para mercados emergentes y para personas que adquirían su primer equipo móvil.
Los siguientes dígitos señalaban la generación o el factor de forma dentro de esa familia. Al tratarse del modelo fundacional de la nueva estrategia de teléfonos ultrabaratos, recibió el número 100, que marcó el inicio y la línea base de toda esa serie.
El Nokia 1100 fue diseñado en el centro de diseño de Nokia en California, a cargo del diseñador búlgaro Manti Makkonen. articles.title: La detección de un fallo de 8 km en una ciudad china reconcilia con la ciencia uno de los eclipses más antiguos de la historia
articles.summary:
Unos científicos han encontrado un fallo en uno de los registros más antiguos que existen de un eclipse solar total. Con la resolución de este error, se abre la puerta a una comprensión mucho mejor de la época en la que tuvo lugar, tanto a nivel histórico como astronómico. Además, se apoya de nuevo algo que ya sabíamos: la Tierra se está frenando y su rotación sucede cada vez más despacio.
17 de julio de 709 a.C. Aquel día, quienes se encontraban en la ciudad china de Qufu vieron cómo se hacía de noche de repente y cuando no tocaba. El fenómeno quedó registrado en una crónica conocida como “Anales de primavera y otoño”, donde se señalaba que el Sol había quedado totalmente eclipsado. Este escrito se convirtió en uno de los registros más antiguos que existen de un eclipse solar total.

articles.summary:
Most data centers and servers on the planet could be vulnerable to dangerous UEFI firmware flaw — here's what we know
A critical buffer overflow vulnerability was found in EDK II, with patch code already available
- Researchers uncover critical UEFI firmware flaw that could enable remote code execution on servers
- Public release of patch code may accelerate exploit development before many vendors deploy updates
- Delayed firmware patching across hardware ecosystems leaves organizations exposed despite available fixes
Cybersecurity researchers from Anthropic and Google have discovered a critical-severity vulnerability in boot-time firmware used by practically every server in existence today.
A patch is available, but given the fragmented market of UEFI manufacturers, it could take months before most of the servers are secured. In the meantime, patch code was made publicly available, which means cybercriminals will have their work laid out for them.
Discovering the bug
Virtually all modern servers today run UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface), software built into the server’s motherboard that helps start the device and load the operating system. It includes security features like Secure Boot, which helps stop unauthorized programs from running when the machine starts.
The free, open source toolkit developers use to build this firmware is called TianoCore EDK II - it serves as a common foundation for creating UEFI firmware for different types of hardware.

A few cracks does not a crisis make
In my review of Apple's iPhone Duo, I noted the engineering and build quality, how easy it is to unfold the phone, and also how solid and sure it feels when you close it. And I have opened and closed the flexible, dual-screen phone many, many times.
When a small set of iPhone Duo owners complained that their large inner screens had unexpectedly and disturbingly cracked, Apple did something unusual: it acknowledged the complaints: "We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement.”
That's not Apple saying there's a fundamental flaw or that the issue is found on anything more than a small number of the already popular phones.
I watched with some dismay as people started bandying about the 'crackgate' phrase. Apple has had its share of 'gates' over the years, including 'bendgate' with the iPhone 6 Plus, and Antenna Gate with the iPhone 4. On the latter, Steve Jobs memorably told customers they were holding the phone wrong (he later apologized for the issues).

articles.title: Cómo saber qué aplicaciones usan el micrófono del celular y bloquear los permisos que no necesitan
articles.summary:
Revisar qué aplicaciones usan el micrófono del celular y bloquear los permisos innecesarios permite reducir el riesgo que datos, conversaciones o hábitos de uso queden expuestos. Los teléfonos actuales muestran señales cuando una app activa este sensor, pero la protección depende también de que cada usuario revise con frecuencia las autorizaciones concedidas.
El acceso al micrófono es necesario para algunas funciones: llamadas, notas de voz, videoconferencias y grabaciones. Sin embargo, una aplicación que no necesita capturar audio para cumplir su tarea puede representar una señal de alerta. La clave está en comprobar si los permisos solicitados guardan relación con el servicio que ofrece.
Los permisos permiten acceder a funciones sensibles
Cuando se instala una aplicación, el sistema operativo puede solicitar permiso para usar recursos del dispositivo. Uber, por ejemplo, necesita acceder a la ubicación para ofrecer sus servicios. Las plataformas de mensajería, las redes sociales y las herramientas de videollamadas pueden requerir acceso a cámara, micrófono o galería de fotos.
El problema aparece cuando una app aparentemente sencilla solicita funciones que no necesita. Una linterna, un juego básico o una herramienta de edición de texto no deberían requerir permiso para grabar audio, leer mensajes o utilizar la cámara.

¿Quién? Hace unas décadas, detrás de Lao Gan Ma apenas había un puesto de fideos. A Tao le ha generado una fortuna estimada en más de 1.000 millones de dólares y a la marca le ha reportado en torno al 55% del segmento de salsa de chili en el país. Voilà une histoire qui devrait rappeler aux utilisateurs d'IA que cet outil doit toujours être utilisé avec parcimonie et méfiance dans bien des domaines. Celui du droit est concerné dans le sujet qui nous intéresse aujourd'hui.
Marie-Line X, a saisi le tribunal administratif de Rennes fin 2025. Sa demande concernait, dans les grandes lignes, le montant de ses impôts lié à la TVA. Non seulement le tribunal ne lui a pas donné raison, mais lui a également infligé une amende de 500 €, notamment à cause de son utilisation de l'intelligence artificielle.
L'abus (d'IA) peut déboucher sur une amende
Dans une ordonnance datée du 19 août 2026 rendue publique, le juge note tout d'abord que la requête n'a pas été précédée d'une réclamation au service territorial de la direction générale des finances publiques, comme il doit en être.
Ensuite, il souligne que cette requête a été précédée d'une autre en octobre 2025, dotée "en substance du même objet". De plus, il indique que la seconde requête a été "manifestement écrite à l'aide d'un outil d'intelligence artificielle". Pour ces deux raisons, le juge a estimé la requête abusive, débouchant sur l'amende de 500 €.

articles.title: La NASA quiere parecerse más a SpaceX: "Más misiones, más a menudo"

La NASA quiere lanzar más misiones al espacio, pero se está topando con su propia burocracia. Por eso, el pasado 21 de octubre la directora de la Dirección de Misiones Científicas de la agencia, Nicky Fox, anunció una serie de cambios en su sistema de selección de misiones. Aunque en ningún momento se ha mencionado a SpaceX, con esto buscan acercarse a una filosofía más parecida a la de la compañía de Elon Musk, cuya máxima lleva mucho tiempo siendo: lanzar, lanzar y lanzar.

Por eso, desde ahora en la evaluación inicial se dará más peso al mérito científico, dejando para más tarde la ingeniería y las finanzas. Esto se tendrá en cuenta en las siguientes fases, que dependerán del tamaño de la misión.
Tres tipos. A grandes rasgos, dependiendo de la magnitud de la misión, las misiones de la NASA se pueden dividir en tres tipos: insignia, medianas y pequeñas. Las primeras son las más caras, de varios miles de millones de dólares, y van a ser las menos afectadas por estos cambios. Básicamente, seguirán su procedimiento habitual. articles.title: CXMT to Start HBM3E Mass Production by the End of 2026
articles.summary:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
CXMT to Start HBM3E Mass Production by the End of 2026
CXMT is expected to start mass production of its first-ever HBM memory in the HBM3E form factor. According to an exclusive report from Reuters, this mass production is anticipated to begin within the next two months, meaning CXMT will officially start by the end of the year. Back in August, CXMT began risk production of HBM3E memory. However, the company has struggled with the yield of HBM3E memory modules, and this situation remains similar today, according to the latest report. While we don't have specific performance details, JEDEC's official data for HBM3E indicates a 1,024-bit width and speeds ranging from 9.2 Gbps per pin to 12.4 Gbps, with most standard configurations targeting 9.6 Gbps per pin. The total bandwidth is around 1.2 TB/s, and capacities range from 24 GB using 8-high stacks to 36 GB using 12-high stacks of 24 Gb layers.

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday added two vulnerabilities impacting Adobe Commerce and Magento, and Google's Brotli decoder library to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.
The vulnerabilities are listed below -

articles.title: The touchscreen MacBook Pro uses a 'Tandem OLED' panel — so why is its 'PROLED XDR' display different to the iPad Pro's 'Ultra Retina XDR' Tandem OLED panel? Let's dig into the specs
articles.summary:
What's the tech inside the touchscreen MacBook Pro's 'PROLED XDR' screen? Here's why the 'tandem' OLED panel is important
The first OLED MacBook Pro screen has a weird name — here's what's behind it
Apple has unveiled its first OLED MacBook Pro laptops, and that means we've got a new bit of display branding: PROLED XDR. You can have the laptop in 14-inch or 16-inch variants, pre-orders are open now for shipping on or after the 6th of November — and we've gone hands-on with them. Literally, because they're also the first touchscreen Macs.
The name 'PROLED XDR' is a new piece of jargon that Apple's debuting with this machine. So what actually is it?
The short answer is that it's a 'Tandem OLED' panel, which means that it uses multiple layers of organic light-emitting diodes — in this case, two layers. Two OLED layers are better than one because the result is considerably brighter than a single-layer OLED: you literally have two OLEDs firing per pixel. It also boosts longevity, because each of the two layers doesn't have to work as hard, so they have a longer lifespan and are more likely to avoid burn-in.
Apple has stayed away from OLED for its MacBook Pro displays in the past, and clearly that's changed. According to Apple that's because PROLED XDR "finally" overcomes the traditional limitations of OLED: low and variable brightness, off-axis color shift and the risk of burn-in from displaying the same interface elements, such as toolbars and palettes, whenever the screen is on.…

articles.title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
articles.summary:
The critical Oracle PeopleSoft bug that ShinyHunters has exploited since May is not one flaw but three chained together, the researchers who reported it said this week.
Oracle patched all three under a single identifier, CVE-2026-35273, in June. Its root is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) that reaches an internal management interface because PeopleSoft trusts its own loopback address by default, opening the door to remote code execution without a login.
The breakdown comes from Bobby Gould of the Zero Day Initiative (ZDI), whose team reported the flaw to Oracle.
In its analysis, ZDI said it reported three distinct vulnerabilities across two PeopleSoft components, and that it is working with Oracle to assign a separate CVE to each. As of this week, the one June identifier is still the only one on the record.
CVE-2026-35273 affects PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools versions 8.61 and 8.62, carries a CVSS score of 9.8, and lets an unauthenticated attacker take over the server over the network. Oracle released its fix in an out-of-band security alert on June 10. The flaw is on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
Attackers were already using it before that fix was in place. Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) attribute a campaign to the group it tracks as UNC6240, better known as ShinyHunters, that exploited the flaw between May 27 and June 9, mostly against universities. articles.title: Tailscale Patches SSH Flaws That Could Let Hacked Devices Gain Root Access on Other Servers
articles.summary:
Tailscale has released version 1.104.4 to fix flaws in its built-in SSH server that could let an attacker reach services and files on other servers that only the root user should be able to touch.
The flaws are in how Tailscale SSH forwards network connections, a job the Tailscale background process carries out with root privileges. To use them, an attacker must already control a device that the network's access rules permit to open an SSH session to the target, with forwarding allowed in that rule.
The flaws come from a report called Tailworm, published days before the fix by Erica Windisch of Cyberdione Labs, who tested released versions of the Tailscale client and the self-hosted headscale control server in a lab.
Tailscale SSH decides who can connect using a device's identity and the network's policy file, not a password or key, so an attacker does not need stolen credentials, only a foothold on a device the policy already trusts.
The flaws "don't allow an unauthenticated attacker to connect to arbitrary Tailscale SSH servers," Tailscale said, and an attacker can still reach only the machines the policy file already allows.
Tailscale SSH's server runs only on Linux and the open-source macOS build; the attacker's own device can be any platform.

One step closer to the Terminator? Experts reveal robot with 'real muscles' strong enough to jump, swim and grasp
“Tissue… grown for cyborgs”
- Laboratory-grown muscle tissue has been developed to improve robot dexterity and motion
- Researchers working at ETH Zurich have demonstrated tissue-based muscle actuators that flex
- The actuators enable small robots to jump and swim, as well as walk and grasp
Flesh-covered robots that can walk, jump, swim and move among us may be closer than we think. Researchers working out of ETH Zurich have been busy developing muscle actuators from centimeter-scale living tissue. These muscle actuators are the latest in a design program, and motion has been improved over 10 times compared with previous iterations.
In designing the biohybrid robots, the researchers have found that it isn’t all about the volume of muscle tissue. How the muscle and the bone (or in this case, an “artificial scaffold”) interact is also important.

While attackers employ AI to automate cyberattacks and accelerate vulnerability discovery, defenders are adopting AI to improve threat detection and enhance incident response.

articles.title: Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers
articles.summary:
A critical 16-year-old flaw in EDK II, the open-source code that most hardware makers use to build UEFI firmware, can allow an attacker to run code on a machine before its operating system loads, but only while the machine is booting over the network.
UEFI firmware is the software that runs first when a computer is switched on, before the operating system. An attacker who can reach the machine with a crafted network message during such a network boot can hang the boot, or, with work tailored to the exact firmware build, run their own code before Secure Boot and other startup defenses load.
An attacker needs no password and no existing access to the machine, but does need to reach it over the network during the short window when it is booting this way.
Red Hat and SUSE, which both ship the affected code, rated the flaw as one an attacker exploits from an adjacent network position rather than across the open internet.
TianoCore, the project behind EDK II, published an advisory on October 22 and rated the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, 9.5 out of 10. A code fix exists, but no stable release of EDK II contains it yet, and the advisory still lists no patched version, so most users have nothing to install today.
What the Flaw Lets an Attacker Do
The flaw is a buffer overflow in EDK II's network-boot code, known as PXE. During a PXE boot, a machine loads its startup image from the network instead of from a local disk.
As part of this, the PXE driver listens for ICMP error messages…

articles.title: Researcher Reveals How Logic Bugs Alone Cracked Microsoft Edge in $175,000 Pwn2Own Win
articles.summary:
A chain of logic flaws, with no memory corruption, can turn a malicious web page into code running on a Windows computer outside Microsoft Edge's sandbox, a security researcher has shown.
Orange Tsai of DEVCORE published the full method on October 28, five months after the chain won $175,000 at the Pwn2Own Berlin contest in May. Microsoft fixed the Edge bugs the day after the contest, so an up-to-date browser is not at risk.
A browser sandbox is the wall that keeps a web page's code inside the browser and off the rest of the computer. Breaking out of it, and then running a program, is what turns a web bug into full control of the machine.
Browser escapes like this almost always rely on memory corruption. This one used none. In his write-up, Tsai describes a chain built solely from logic errors in how Edge and Windows handle ordinary features, and he says the whole exploit is under 100 lines of code.
The result is a universal cross-site scripting (UXSS) primitive: a way to run JavaScript on any website, bypassing the content security policy meant to prevent it.
Because the attack starts from the browser's own process, it can reach sites like google.com that an ordinary web bug cannot touch. Tsai calls this a new attack surface rather than a one-off bug.
This was a competition exploit, not an attack seen in the wild. Tsai demonstrated it on stage at Pwn2Own; there is no evidence it has been used against real users, and the public CVE records list exploitation as none. One step …

Could decommissioned nuclear sites really host data centers?
- Nvidia wants to turn Germany's retired nuclear sites into AI data centers
- Germany's nuclear shutdown leaves dozens of former power stations awaiting dismantling
- Nvidia and PreussenElektra are investigating new uses for Germany's retired nuclear facilities
Nvidia has agreed to examine whether shuttered German reactor sites could become computing hubs, though the company rules out restarting any idle units.
The US chipmaker signed a preliminary agreement with PreussenElektra GmbH (PEL), a utility from Germany, to study the idea at decommissioned locations.
The arrangement does not involve generating electricity from fission for any future facility, since the work concentrates on existing grid links and water access.
Reusing sites without reviving reactors
Following the Fukushima incident, Germany permanently closed its final operating reactors in April 2023 and is now dismantling about 30 atomic stations nationwide.
PreussenElektra oversees the closure and teardown of eight of those stations, and these are probably the locations that will receive scrutiny.
Neither company has named the sites under review, so the eight locations managed by PreussenElektra remain an assumption rather than a confirmed list.

articles.title: Volt Typhoon Used Covert Silent Train Network in Four Zero-Day Exploitation Campaigns
articles.summary:
The China-nexus cyber espionage group known as Volt Typhoon has been attributed to a now-disrupted covert access network dubbed Silent Train that has been put to use for zero-day exploitation and strategic access.
"First identified in late 2023, Silent Train uses rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT, and enterprise infrastructure," Lumen Technologies Black Lotus Labs said in a report shared with The Hacker News. "It employs anti-forensic techniques, compartmentalized operations, and post-operation cleanup to minimize detection and attribution."
Its main purpose is to facilitate critical attack phases like vulnerability exploitation, credential access, data exfiltration, and to maintain continued access to victim environments. The activity stands out for two main reasons -
- It singled out entities that could provide scalable access to downstream customers, sensitive networks, or strategic programs.
- It targeted endpoint management platforms, network management systems, SD-WAN orchestrators, and control plane technologies that play a crucial role within enterprise environments.
Hundreds of victims have been identified across telecommunications providers, government, defense contractors, satellite and mission-critical communication services, universities, IT firms, and critical infrastructure such as water, energy, transportation, maritime, rail, aviation, and emergency services.

articles.title: Cómo evitar que la IA cree un perfil detallado con tus datos dispersos en internet
articles.summary:
La inteligencia artificial puede reunir datos dispersos en internet, vincular cuentas y construir un perfil detallado de una persona a partir de publicaciones, correos electrónicos, fotos y otros rastros digitales. Este proceso, asociado al doxing, puede exponer identidades, facilitar el acoso y aumentar el riesgo de robo de cuentas, chantaje o daños reputacionales.
La advertencia cobra importancia porque las herramientas actuales reducen el tiempo y el coste necesarios para relacionar información pública. Kaspersky explica que los sistemas de IA pueden automatizar búsquedas en fuentes abiertas, revisar bases de datos filtradas y conectar pistas que antes requerían muchas horas de investigación manual.
La empresa de ciberseguridad recomienda reducir los vínculos entre datos personales para dificultar la reconstrucción de una identidad.
La IA puede unir publicaciones, fotos y cuentas aparentemente separadas
El doxing consiste en localizar, cotejar y difundir datos personales sin consentimiento. Durante años, esta práctica dependió de búsquedas manuales y herramientas de inteligencia de fuentes abiertas, conocidas como OSINT. La IA generativa añade una capa de automatización: analiza grandes cantidades de información y detecta relaciones entre nombres de usuario, direcciones de correo electrónico, publicaciones y perfiles.

articles.title: Attackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Internet-Exposed Palo Alto Networks Management Interfaces
articles.summary:
Palo Alto Networks on Wednesday warned that threat actors are exploiting the recently patched PHP2Shell vulnerabilities against publicly-accessible management interfaces.
"Active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet," the network security company said in an update to its advisory.
The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS scores: 9.2), allow attackers to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on systems running affected versions of PHP. The issues were patched upstream by the PHP Foundation on October 21, 2026, in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35.
The development comes days after Israeli cybersecurity company Dream said it observed a suspected China-nexus threat actor weaponizing the flaws in conjunction with a local privilege escalation bug in the Linux kernel, tracked as Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300, CVSS score: 7.8), to root 25 servers across the U.S., Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea.
Among those were three systems belonging to a U.S. government-affiliated environment.
"The affected devices run specific versions of a large vendor's firewall software," Dream noted. "The attacker then launched attacks against Active Directory. The recovered artifacts confirm credential extraction and directory enumeration."

articles.summary:

The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-41709 (CVSS score: 2.7), an insufficient logging vulnerability that could permit a malicious actor with admin access to perform certain operations without being logged.

- VMware Cloud Foundation SXi-9.1.0.0-25370933 and ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025

- VMware ESX ESXi80U3j-25429389
- VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.4
- VMware Telco Cloud Platform ESXi80U3j-25429389

These are the conclusions of research by Trend Micro’s AI cybersecurity unit TrendAI, whose researchers analyzed troves of digital advertising data. The research found that Israeli company Discover-Tech was the number one bidder on Starlink advertising traffic.

Starlink users surveilled by ads

articles.title: Vous pensiez télécharger ChatGPT ou Claude ? Des pirates ont glissé un malware dans de faux installateurs
articles.summary:
Le fichier d’installation porte bien la signature d’OpenAI ou d’Anthropic, mais l’archive téléchargée depuis de faux dépôts GitHub contient aussi un fichier piégé. Les pirates l’utilisent pour faire miner de la cryptomonnaie à votre ordinateur, à votre insu.
Les pirates de la campagne Yoba ont mis en ligne sur GitHub de faux projets d’applications de bureau pour les derniers modèles d’OpenAI et d’Anthropic. Google affichait certains de ces dépôts en tête de ses résultats, probablement grâce à un empoisonnement du référencement, selon Check Point Research, qui suit la campagne depuis deux mois. Pour tromper les internautes, les pirates ont glissé leur fichier malveillant juste à côté d’un programme d’installation authentique, signé par OpenAI ou Anthropic.
Un vrai installateur signé, pour charger le fichier piégé
En cherchant GPT-5.6 Sol, des internautes pouvaient par exemple atterrir sur le dépôt gpt-5-6/sol-free-desktop, puis sur la page gpt-5-6.github.io, avec un lien vers une archive ZIP. Les pirates n’ont même pas pris la peine de gonfler la popularité de ces projets avec de fausses étoiles ou de fausses copies sur GitHub.
Un programme Windows a besoin de fichiers DLL au lancement, et ces bibliothèques sont souvent cherchées en premier dans son dossier. Les pirates ont donc déposé un faux fichier winmm.dll à côté du Setup.exe signé. articles.title: Pokémon Unite : c'est (bientôt) fini pour ce jeu Pokémon, qui fermera ses portes dans quelques mois
articles.summary:
Trente ans plus tard, la « folie Pokémon » continue de battre son plein, mais tous les jeux de la franchise ne connaissent pas le même succès. Pokémon Unite s’apprête à tirer sa révérence en 2027, après plusieurs années de combats en équipe sur mobile et Nintendo Switch.
La licence Pokémon a beau fêter ses 30 ans en 2026, elle n’a clairement pas l’intention de ralentir. Entre les cartes à collectionner qui s’arrachent et les fans prêts à patienter des heures pour obtenir leur précieux sésame, l’engouement reste intact. Pourtant, du côté de Pokémon Unite, le compte à rebours est bel et bien lancé.
Pokémon Unite prépare son dernier combat
Lancé en 2021, Pokémon Unite proposait une formule différente des jeux Pokémon traditionnels, avec un MOBA (pour Multiplayer Online Battle Arena) dans lequel deux équipes de cinq joueurs s’affrontent pour marquer un maximum de points, en incarnant leurs créatures favorites. Accessible sur Nintendo Switch et sur smartphones, le titre entendait séduire aussi bien les amateurs de Pokémon que les adeptes de combats compétitifs.
Mais l’aventure a désormais une date de fin. Comme le rapporte notamment Kotaku, les serveurs du jeu fermeront leurs portes le 23 mars 2027. Une échéance qui laisse encore un peu de temps aux joueurs pour profiter de leurs dernières parties, mais qui marque la fin programmée de ce spin-off qui dépassait les 70 millions de téléchargements un peu avant son premier anniversaire, en avril 2022.

articles.title: FADU wants to take the CPU out of AI storage by putting the file system inside the SSD, but the proof won't arrive until 2027
articles.summary:
FADU wants to take the CPU out of AI storage by putting the file system inside the SSD, but the proof won't arrive until 2027
But samples won't land until Q3 2027
- FADU's File-Semantic SSD runs path lookup, permission checks, and file-to-flash mapping in firmware instead of on the host
- NFSv3 requests ride inside standard NVMe commands, so GPUs, DPUs, and remote clients can reach files without requiring a host file system
- Its headline 460,000 ops/s result came from a PCIe 5.0 host, with PCIe 6.0 results promised by Q1 2027
South Korean controller designer FADU has shown off an SSD that understands files rather than just blocks, betting that the next bottleneck in AI storage is not raw bandwidth but the CPU time spent working out where data lives.
The File-Semantic SSD (FS-SSD), unveiled at the OCP Global Summit, moves file lookup, access checks and file-to-address translation into firmware on FADU's sixth-generation controller.
FADU's whitepaper promises GPUs, DPUs and network cards a route to their files with "no host filesystem, no block layer, and no storage-server CPU in the path." Partner samples are not expected until Q3 2027.
Not the first approach to the 'CPU problem'
FADU is no newcomer to data center flash. Its Gen5 controller sits in the SN861, which Western Digital launched and SanDisk now sells; last year, the company said it had signed controller supply deals with two of the four hyperscalers, weeks after revealing its Sierra PCIe 6.0 controller.

articles.title: Un joueur sur trois pourrait craquer pour GTA 6, tout simplement du jamais vu pour un jeu vidéo !
articles.summary:
GTA 6 n'est pas encore en rayon, et il est déjà entré dans l'histoire. Selon le cabinet Circana, 29 % des joueurs américains sur console et PC comptent acheter le titre de Rockstar Games, un niveau jamais mesuré pour un jeu vidéo.
À quelques semaines de sa sortie officielle, prévue le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, GTA 6 décroche un record d'intention d'achat aux États-Unis. Après treize ans d'attente, un GTA V qui n'a jamais quitté les classements après avoir lui-même battu des records à son époque notamment en France, et des précommandes qui se comptent en millions, il faut vivre sur Mars, pour qui s'intéresse même de loin aux jeux vidéo, pour ne pas voir l'engouement. Le jeu de Rockstar s'annonce ainsi comme l'une des plus grosses sorties de l'histoire du divertissement, et comme un moteur des ventes de consoles pour les fêtes, selon une étude publiée ce 28 octobre par le cabinet américain Circana.
Un niveau d'attente record pour GTA 6
Le cabinet d'études Circana fournit des données de marché aux fabricants et aux distributeurs. Son outil PlayerPulse suit notamment l'intention d’achat des joueurs américains sur console et sur PC, c'est-à-dire la part d'entre eux qui déclarent vouloir acheter un jeu donné. Pour GTA 6, elle atteint 29 %, soit près d’un joueur sur trois. Jamais un jeu vidéo n'avait obtenu un tel score dans les relevés du cabinet.
